add.title: Self-Respect Movement – Chengalpattu 1929, Self-Respect Marriages and the Andhra Echo
add.md:
# Self-Respect Movement (Suyamariyathai Iyakkam) – Course and Andhra Echo
- **Founder and year:** **E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)**, **1925**, after leaving the Congress over the **Cheranmadevi Gurukulam** caste-dining row and communal representation.
  - Organ: **Kudi Arasu** (Tamil weekly, from **2 May 1925**); English **Revolt** (1928); later **Viduthalai**.
- **Background:** Periyar led the **Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25)** in Travancore for Dalits' right to use temple roads → title **"Vaikom Veerar"**.
- **First Provincial Self-Respect Conference:** **Chengalpattu (Chingleput), February 1929**, presided by **W.P.A. Soundarapandian**.
  - Resolutions: abolish caste titles and caste marks, **equal property and inheritance rights for women**, women's right to divorce, raise marriage age / end child marriage, widow remarriage, reservation for lower castes.
- **Self-respect marriages (from 1928):** no Brahmin priest, no Sanskrit mantras, often inter-caste and widow marriages.
  - Legalised by the **Hindu Marriage (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1967** – new **Section 7-A** – under **C.N. Annadurai's DMK** government.
- **Ideas:** **rationalism**, atheism, anti-caste, anti-Brahmin priesthood, women's emancipation; Periyar toured the **USSR (1931-32)** and briefly worked with socialists.
- **Title "Periyar":** given at the **Tamil Nadu Women's Conference, Madras, November 1938**.
- **Relation with the Justice Party:** after the Justice Party's 1937 defeat Periyar became its president (1938); at the **Salem conference, 1944** it was renamed **Dravidar Kazhagam**; the **DMK** split away in **1949** (Annadurai).
- **Centenary:** the movement completed **100 years in 2025**; Tamil Nadu marked the centenary.
- **Andhra echo (AP angle):**
  - **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary ("Kavi Raju", Tenali)** – the Andhra voice of the same rationalist, anti-Puranic, non-Brahmin critique: **Suta Puranam**, **Shambuka Vadha**; he too promoted priest-less marriages.
  - **Gora (Goparaju Ramachandra Rao)** – **Atheist Centre**, Mudunuru 1940 → Vijayawada 1947; inter-caste marriages and work in Dalit colonies.
  - Dalit leaders **Bhagya Reddy Varma** and **Jala Rangaswamy** drew on the same ideas for the **Adi-Andhra/Adi-Hindu** identity.
  - In Andhra the non-Brahmin current stayed mostly with the **Justice Party** and **rationalist writers**; Periyar's Dravidian separatism found little support among Telugus.
> Trap: Self-Respect Movement = Periyar, 1925 (not Ambedkar or Narayana Guru); first conference Chengalpattu 1929; Section 7-A legalised self-respect marriages in 1967; Suta Puranam = Tripuraneni, not Periyar.
~~ Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-Respect_Movement; Vision IAS "100 Years of the Self-Respect Movement" (2025); Vajiram & Ravi; GKToday; app notes 1:154
